item_name: KMP mobile implementation and execution skills
classification: A minimal, execution-oriented stack: official Google Android skills and Android CLI for Android work; official JetBrains Kotlin skills for KMP migrations and Kotlin/Native build performance; one conditional iOS execution integration; and selectively adapted community KMP guidance. These are complementary, not substitutes for Gradle/Xcode builds or real-device BLE validation.

candidates.candidate: Google Android skills plus Android CLI
candidates.kind: Official Google skill pack and CLI
candidates.adopt: Primary Android foundation. Install android-cli, then add testing-setup, perfetto-trace-analysis, r8-analyzer, and play-policy-insights only when their trigger applies.
candidates.why: The CLI covers SDK/AVD management, project creation, APK deployment, screen/layout inspection, documentation lookup, and skill management. The targeted skills add Android testing, trace analysis, shrinker analysis, and release-policy audit workflows.

candidates.adopt: Install on demand: kotlin-tooling-native-build-performance for slow iOS/Kotlin-Native builds; kotlin-tooling-agp9-migration and kotlin-tooling-cocoapods-spm-migration only during their named migrations.
candidates.why: They cover KMP-specific Gradle restructuring, CocoaPods-to-SwiftPM transition, and measured Kotlin/Native build-performance work that the Android pack does not cover.

candidates.adopt: Use only inside an Xcode 27-capable macOS environment, especially device-interaction, test-modernizer, and audit-xcode-security-settings. Do not duplicate them globally for every agent.
candidates.why: Apple documents Xcode-built specialists and agent skill/plugin support; this is the lowest-provenance-risk option when the team works in Xcode itself.

candidates.candidate: XcodeBuildMCP with its optional xcodebuildmcp skill
candidates.adopt: Conditional iOS execution path for Codex or Claude outside Xcode. Enable simulator workflows first; enable device, debugger, and UI automation workflows only when the team has approved signing and physical-device access.
candidates.why: It gives a single session-aware interface for discover/build/run/test/log/LLDB/UI automation across simulators and signed devices, rather than maintaining a large custom xcodebuild and simctl prompt.

candidates.adopt: Adapt or selectively install only kotlin-platform-kmp-bridges, kotlin-testing-kmp, and kotlin-project-bugfix after review. Do not install its full pipeline, hooks, settings, or GitHub workflows as a baseline.
candidates.why: The small skills add source-set/expect-actual boundary, KMP test, and root-cause guidance; the full 14-skill orchestration bundle would duplicate existing agent workflows and increase maintenance/context surface.

candidates.candidate: Broad community Compose kits such as felipechaux/kmp-compose-multiplatform-skill and haidrrrry/compose-kotlin-agent-skills
candidates.adopt: Avoid as a default installation. Mine individual rules only if they match the repository's existing architecture.
candidates.why: They are useful signals of current Compose practices, but impose opinionated architecture or strict MVI assumptions and have much thinner independent validation than the official packs.

coverage:
| Candidate | Create/build/run | Debug/test/performance | Sign/release/publish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Android CLI + official skills | Create projects; manage SDK/AVD; deploy APKs; Gradle remains the build authority | Layout/screenshot/ADB-oriented inspection; testing setup; Perfetto; R8 | Policy and billing-adjacent guidance only; no complete Play publishing workflow |
| JetBrains Kotlin skills | KMP Gradle and iOS integration migrations; Kotlin/Native build tuning | Measured native build diagnosis | No signing, archive, store, or device-QA workflow |
| Apple Xcode 27 skills | Xcode-local Swift/UI/device workflows | Device interaction, testing modernization, security settings | No evidence of end-to-end store-publishing automation |
| XcodeBuildMCP | Discover/build/run/test on simulator and signed physical device | Logs, LLDB, screenshots, hierarchy, UI automation | Requires Xcode signing; no replacement for App Store approval/publishing controls |
| Selected community KMP skills | Architecture, source sets, bug fixing, KMP tests | Guidance only; must invoke native tools and devices | No release authority |
platform_support: Android: the Android CLI and official skills are strongest for SDK, emulator, APK deployment, UI inspection, Android tests, Perfetto, and R8. KMP/common code: JetBrains skills cover AGP 9 KMP structure, SwiftPM migration, and Kotlin/Native compilation performance. iOS: full Xcode on macOS is still required; use Apple Xcode 27 skills in Xcode or XcodeBuildMCP for external-agent simulator/device execution. Physical Android and iOS devices remain necessary for Bluetooth behavior, permission prompts, background transitions, pairing, and connection recovery.
bluetooth_relevance: No inspected official Android, JetBrains Kotlin, Apple Xcode, or selected community skill is a dependable BLE/KMP implementation skill. Android CLI can deploy and inspect an app on a connected Android device, and XcodeBuildMCP can run/log a signed iOS build, but neither models GATT/CoreBluetooth state, permissions, background behavior, or hardware protocol truth. Keep one small repository-local BLE skill/workflow with KMP interfaces in common code, Android and CoreBluetooth implementations at platform edges, serialized operations, redacted logs, and a required hardware-in-the-loop test matrix. Emulator and simulator success must never count as BLE proof.
toolchain_and_prerequisites: Android requires a JDK compatible with the project, Gradle wrapper, Android SDK/platform tools, ADB, an emulator or physical Android device, and BLE hardware for final validation. JetBrains CocoaPods-to-SwiftPM migration requires Kotlin 2.4.0-Beta2 or later, Xcode 16.4 or later, and careful Gradle plus Xcode verification. iOS execution requires macOS and full Xcode; XcodeBuildMCP additionally requires macOS 14.5 or later, Xcode 16 or later, and Node.js 18 or later when installed through npm. Signed device work additionally needs an Apple team, bundle ID/profiles/certificates, a trusted device, Developer Mode, and user-controlled physical-device actions. Android CLI does not replace Gradle; XcodeBuildMCP does not replace Xcode signing configuration.
installation_or_adoption: Use project-local, task-triggered installation rather than a global catalog. Android: `android skills add --skill=android-cli --project=.` and add one named specialist only when needed; avoid `--all`. Kotlin: use the Kotlin marketplace/plugin or `npx skills add Kotlin/kotlin-agent-skills`, then retain only the three named KMP skills needed by the project. iOS: choose exactly one execution route per environment: Apple built-ins within Xcode 27, or XcodeBuildMCP for external agents. As observed on 2026-07-26, android/skills had 6,358 GitHub stars, Kotlin/kotlin-agent-skills 967, XcodeBuildMCP 6,148, mmiani 56, and felipechaux 66; these are adoption signals, not quality or user-satisfaction evidence.
evidence_of_maintenance: Google's Android skills repository is official, actively updated, and its Android documentation was updated in July 2026. JetBrains documents Kotlin AI skills, supports Codex and Claude Code, and the Kotlin agent-skill repository had activity in July 2026. XcodeBuildMCP is active, MIT licensed, has CI, and showed July 2026 repository activity. The community KMP catalogs were created in March 2026 and showed July metadata updates, but their comparatively small communities and limited independent feedback justify a trial-only posture.
public_user_feedback:
| Candidate | Relevant public feedback | Decision impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Android CLI skill | A user reported stale `android screen` examples against Android CLI 1.0 in issue #74; another reported that its imperative `curl | bash` guidance can cause an agent to attempt a system-wide install without explicit consent in issue #61. | Verify command syntax with `android ... --help`; treat CLI installation as a user-approved prerequisite. |
| JetBrains Kotlin skills | No meaningful user review of the KMP migration/native-performance skills was found in the inspected official repository. Issue #17 requests a Coroutines skill, which indicates a catalog gap rather than product validation. | Use the official skills for their narrow documented triggers, not as a complete KMP engineering playbook. |
| XcodeBuildMCP | A detailed user report in issue #492 describes intermittent planning hangs and stale multiple MCP-server processes; the reporter recommends a single instance, timeouts, and a direct `xcodebuild | tee` fallback. | Enable one server per workspace/session, set time limits, and retain direct Xcode commands as a recovery path. |
| Community KMP/Compose kits | A Reddit user said the felipechaux KMP Compose skill felt solid, while the mmiani author describes existing KMP skills as often generic, thin, or overly opinionated. This is anecdotal and not an independent benchmark. | Do not adopt a broad community bundle on this evidence alone; selectively adapt small, reviewable rules. |
security_and_release_safety: Never place Android keystores, key passwords, Apple private keys, provisioning profiles, App Store Connect keys, Play service-account JSON, or device identifiers in skills, prompts, logs, or repository history. Separate build/verification authority from release authority: agents may assemble and validate unsigned/debug artifacts, but archive/export/upload/store-track changes require explicit approval and least-privilege CI secrets. For XcodeBuildMCP and Appium-style device tools, start with simulator-only permissions; enable device workflows only after signing assets are already configured and never give the agent raw credential contents. Add a release checklist that verifies package/application ID, version/build number, signing identity fingerprint, privacy manifest/data-safety changes, store metadata, and a real-device BLE smoke result before upload.
limitations_and_gaps: The official Android pack is new and intentionally targeted; it does not provide a complete Gradle, Play publishing, BLE, or KMP release skill. Android CLI documentation/examples have shown syntax drift, and it must not be allowed to auto-install system software without approval. Kotlin's CocoaPods-to-SwiftPM workflow is a migration skill using experimental-era prerequisites, not a general iOS integration substitute. Apple Xcode skills are tied to a current Xcode environment. XcodeBuildMCP is powerful but adds an MCP server, telemetry considerations, failure modes, and potential hangs; it should remain optional. None of these packages validates real BLE radio behavior, vendor protocol framing, reconnection, or background behavior without hardware.
recommendation: Priority 1: add a project-local Android execution entry point using the official Android CLI skill and keep Gradle/ADB commands in the repository guide. Priority 2: add only the official Android testing and performance skills when the task specifically triggers them. Priority 3: install JetBrains Kotlin Native Build Performance; keep AGP 9 and CocoaPods-to-SwiftPM skills dormant until a migration is actually scheduled. Priority 4: pick one iOS execution mechanism: Xcode 27's built-ins for Xcode-centric work, otherwise XcodeBuildMCP with simulator-only defaults and a direct xcodebuild fallback. Priority 5: adapt a tiny KMP platform-bridge and test workflow from mmiani into repository-local instructions, then add the dedicated BLE/release workflow separately. Do not install any large all-in-one Compose/KMP catalog, Appium real-device stack, or broad global plugin unless a concrete task requires it.
